title: The Concept of Quantum Superposition
text:
In quantum physics, superposition describes the principle that a physical system can exist in multiple states simultaneously. Before measurement occurs, a particle's state is not fixed; rather, it is described by a combination of all potential states defined within its wave function.

The act of observation fundamentally alters this state. Measurement forces the wave function to collapse, compelling the particle into one definite outcome from the range of possibilities. This transition from probabilistic existence to concrete reality represents one of quantum mechanics' most counterintuitive features and remains central to current theoretical debates about measurement theory.
